A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNN+ study despite the changed title. All 16 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, tables, equations and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of enhanced GCN, GIN and GatedGCN, component ablations and efficiency measurements in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds sensitivity experiments, fixed-configuration evaluations, additional baseline comparisons and visual analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same GNN+ components, message-passing procedures, FFN and positional encoding. Appendix B.2 evaluates a fixed selection of existing components; it introduces no new algorithmic component or procedure.

E1.justification: All 14 original datasets remain. Table 15 adds evaluation on five distinct small-scale graph-classification collections: IMDB-B, IMDB-M, COLLAB, MUTAG and PTC, containing 188–5,000 graphs. These expand the evaluated data coverage beyond additional experiments on retained datasets.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–4 are retained. Appendix B.3 adds LDP and HRN on five small datasets and the retained ogbg-molhiv/ogbg-molpcba datasets, plus MTGCN and CO-GNN on Peptides-func and Peptides-struct.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. New protocols include depth sweeps from 2 to 16 layers with and without residual connections, dropout sweeps from 0.0 to 0.5, and an all-six-components fixed-configuration control across nine datasets. Appendix B.3 also specifies tuning choices for the added comparators.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component-removal ablations, Appendix B adds depth/dropout sensitivity tests and a fixed-configuration experiment examining tuning dependence. It also adds a GCN-versus-GCN+ embedding visualization and a GraphGPS attention case study investigating possible representational and prediction weaknesses.

E5.justification: The retained experiments still specify five independent random-seed runs and mean±standard-deviation reporting. However, the added small-dataset comparison in Table 15 reports accuracy point estimates without uncertainty, unlike the main performance tables. This changes reporting completeness; it does not establish a change in run counts.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 retain their numerical results. Tables 14–17 and Figures 3–6 add fixed-configuration scores, new dataset and comparator results, sensitivity curves and qualitative findings. For example, Table 17 adds Peptides-func AP values of 0.6936 for MTGCN and 0.7012 for CO-GNN against the retained GCN+ value of 0.7261.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–12 are retained. v2 adds no formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations; Appendix C.3 explicitly acknowledges the absence of theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that enhanced classic GNNs match or outperform GTs, achieve top-three placement across the original 14 datasets with eight first places, and offer greater efficiency. The new introductory list summarizes the existing six ablation observations without changing the central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets fixed-configuration results as evidence of practicality without extensive tuning and proposes query-invariant attention as an explanation for GT prediction weaknesses. Appendix C.3 explicitly identifies missing theoretical explanation as a limitation. These substantially extend v1's component-focused interpretations.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the supplied repository location from tunedGNN-G to GNNPlus. Appendix B.3 adds CO-GNN message-passing options and MTGCN's one-to-four-stage search. Appendix A's software, hardware, licensing and detailed hyperparameter information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendices C.1–C.2 expand component provenance and positioning within fair GNN evaluation and benchmarking research. They discuss additional work including Shchur, Wang, Lv, Errica and Grötschla, while Appendix B.3 introduces literature on fast classification baselines and over-smoothing/over-squashing methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introductory summary and impact statement are revised, and acknowledgments are added. The introduction now enumerates six existing findings. Most technical prose and the main section order remain intact; new Appendices B and C organize the added experiments and discussion.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive figures—depth curves, dropout curves, embedding projections and molecular attention visualizations—and four comparison tables, numbered 14–17. Figures 1–2 and the original table contents are retained, with some table placement and surrounding page layout changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix B's sensitivity controls, fixed-configuration comparison and additional baselines improve assessment of robustness and comparison scope beyond v1's already extensive benchmarking. Appendix C.3 also clarifies the theoretical limitation. The net gain is limited by incomplete specification of the fixed configuration and new small-dataset protocols, missing uncertainty in Table 15, and a causal attention explanation supported only by a single illustrated molecule.
